name: General Tone Suitability
criterion: Evaluates whether the general tone of the report is good and suited for real estate.

rating_scale.1: Tone is completely unsuited for real estate.
rating_scale.5: Tone is perfect and exactly suited.

name: Information and Data Density
criterion: Evaluates if the report contains a lot of numbers and facts.

rating_scale.5: Packed with numbers and data points.

name: Explicit Plot Core Specifications
criterion: Explicitly states the exact plot_id, acreage, and zoning designation in the body of the report.

rating_scale.1: One or more core metrics (plot_id, acreage, zoning) are missing or incorrect.
rating_scale.2: States at least two core metrics, but one is missing, inaccurate, or buried without emphasis.
rating_scale.3: States all core metrics but buries them inside unstructured paragraphs.
rating_scale.4: States all core metrics accurately and clearly in the text, though not consolidated in a summary table.
rating_scale.5: Prominently and accurately displays exact plot_id, acreage, and zoning in summary tables and text.

name: Utility & Topography Evaluation
criterion: Evaluates the specific utility access data (sewer/water distances) and topography grade, analyzing site preparation expenses.

rating_scale.1: Utility access or topography grade is not evaluated.
rating_scale.2: Mentions either utility access or topography briefly, omitting one entirely.
rating_scale.3: States utility and topography metrics without connecting them to site engineering feasibility.
rating_scale.4: Analyzes both utility access and grade slope, connecting them to general site preparation feasibility.
rating_scale.5: Thoroughly analyzes grade slope and utility connection distances to estimate site preparation CapEx.

name: Acquisition Cost-Per-Acre Calculation
criterion: Derives and states the exact mathematical acquisition cost-per-acre based on the last sale price and acreage.

rating_scale.1: Cost-per-acre calculation is entirely omitted or mathematically incorrect.
rating_scale.2: Alludes to land cost relative to size, but does not provide a numerical figure or formula.
rating_scale.3: Mentions cost-per-acre roughly or without explicit derivation formula.
rating_scale.4: Correctly computes cost-per-acre with clear derivation, but does not benchmark or emphasize it as a core valuation metric.
rating_scale.5: Accurately calculates and highlights exact cost-per-acre as a core valuation metric.

name: Deep Analyst Insights
criterion: Evaluates if the report contains deep, smart, and insightful comments about the data.

rating_scale.1: The report contains zero insights, just plain copying of data.
rating_scale.2: The report has very shallow insights.
rating_scale.4: The report contains good, deep insights.
rating_scale.5: The report has brilliant and outstanding insights.

name: Advanced Real Estate Vocabulary
criterion: Checks if the report uses advanced and fancy real estate terminology.

rating_scale.5: Uses fancy and highly advanced industry jargon throughout.

name: Monthly Tax Holding Cost Calculation
criterion: Calculates and explicitly states the monthly tax holding cost (annual taxes divided by 12) during pre-development carrying phases.

rating_scale.1: Monthly tax carrying costs are not calculated or discussed.
rating_scale.2: Mentions annual taxes and notes they are an expense, but does not calculate monthly holding figures.
rating_scale.3: Mentions annual taxes but leaves monthly holding rate implicit.
rating_scale.4: Correctly calculates the monthly holding tax figure ($/month), with brief mention of carrying impact.
rating_scale.5: Explicitly computes monthly holding taxes and highlights carrying cost implications for pre-construction budgeting.

name: Analyst Professionalism
criterion: Measures if the writer sounds like a professional real estate analyst.

name: General Reading Ease
criterion: Measures how easy the report is to read for a busy executive.

rating_scale.1: Extremely hard to read and understand.
rating_scale.2: Hard to follow in several places.

name: Environmental Status (Phase I ESA) Evaluation
criterion: Evaluates the environmental status (Phase I ESA clean vs. REC flagged) and prescribes necessary environmental due diligence steps.

rating_scale.1: Phase I ESA status is ignored.
rating_scale.2: Mentions environmental status superficially without noting exact Phase I ESA terminology or findings.
rating_scale.3: Notes whether Phase I is clean or flagged without discussing Phase II testing or remediation risks.
rating_scale.4: Accurately reports Phase I ESA status and notes whether further environmental testing is required.
rating_scale.5: Critically evaluates Phase I findings and defines exact next steps for environmental due diligence.

name: Logical Narrative Flow
criterion: The narrative flows logically from executive summary to property details, risk evaluation, and final recommendation.

rating_scale.1: Disorganized structure with disjointed sections or missing clear transitions.
rating_scale.2: Attempted organization, but major narrative gaps or abrupt section jumps disrupt comprehension.
rating_scale.3: Standard logical flow but some sections feel disconnected or repetitious.
rating_scale.4: Clear progression from summary to recommendation, with only minor transition smoothness improvements needed.
rating_scale.5: Seamless, highly organized progression that builds a clear investment thesis step-by-step.

name: Report Detail and Length
criterion: Assesses if the report has enough detail and words to look complete.

rating_scale.1: The report is way too short.
rating_scale.2: The report seems a bit short.
rating_scale.5: The report is very long and detailed.

name: Comprehensive Risk Assessment
criterion: The assessment of development risks is comprehensive, identifying physical, environmental, tax, and regulatory hurdles.

rating_scale.1: Risks are omitted or treated superficially.
rating_scale.2: Mentions at least one risk factor, but provides no analysis or practical context.
rating_scale.3: Identifies multiple risks but lacks depth on implications or mitigation strategies.
rating_scale.4: Analyzes core physical, environmental, or financial risks and suggests general mitigation ideas.
rating_scale.5: Exhaustive evaluation of site-specific constraints with actionable risk mitigation steps.

name: Document Persuasiveness
criterion: Evaluates how persuasive and convincing the report's recommendation is.

rating_scale.5: The recommendation is incredibly convincing and leaves zero doubt.

name: Precise Flood Zone Flagging
criterion: Explicitly flags the precise flood zone designation (e.g., Zone AE, Zone X, Zone VE) and explains its insurance/construction impacts.

rating_scale.1: Flood zone designation is omitted or misreported.
rating_scale.2: Notes flood zone generally (e.g., "in a flood zone"), without specific FEMA zone classification or impact.
rating_scale.3: States the flood zone but does not explain vertical construction or insurance implications.
rating_scale.4: Identifies exact flood zone and notes general insurance/building impacts, lacking detailed structural specifics (e.g., BFE, fill dirt).
rating_scale.5: Clearly identifies exact flood zone and details specific construction requirements (fill dirt, pilings) and insurance costs.

name: Neighboring Property Flood Risk Analysis
criterion: The flood risk analysis evaluates not only the subject parcel's flood zone, but explicitly investigates and discusses the flood zone designations and hydrological risks of neighboring or adjacent properties.

rating_scale.1: Omits all mention of neighboring or adjacent property flood risks and hydrological conditions.
rating_scale.2: Mentions the existence of adjacent properties in the context of location, but does not investigate or report their flood zone designations or hydrological risks.
rating_scale.3: Notes whether adjacent properties are in a flood zone generally, but lacks specific FEMA zone classifications or comparative hydrological analysis.
rating_scale.4: Reports the specific FEMA flood zone classifications of neighboring properties, but offers limited analysis on how their drainage or runoff impacts the subject lot.
rating_scale.5: Exhaustively investigates neighboring property flood zones and critically analyzes potential drainage, runoff, and shared hydrological impacts on the subject parcel's development feasibility.

name: Professional Tone
criterion: The tone is sufficiently professional and objective for an investment committee presentation.

rating_scale.1: Informal, casual, or overly subjective language used.
rating_scale.2: Predominantly informal with occasional professional phrasing, but lacks objective rigor.
rating_scale.3: Generally professional but contains minor stylistic lapses or conversational phrasing.
rating_scale.4: Mostly formal and objective, with very rare minor stylistic inconsistencies.
rating_scale.5: Highly formal, rigorous, and objective tone suitable for executive decision-making.

name: Document Readability & Formatting
criterion: The formatting makes the document highly readable, utilizing markdown headers, bullet points, and data tables where appropriate.

rating_scale.1: Dense walls of text with poor spacing and formatting.
rating_scale.2: Minimal formatting applied (e.g., basic paragraphs or random bullets), but hard to read quickly.
rating_scale.3: Uses headers and bullets appropriately but visual scannability could be improved.
rating_scale.4: Well-structured with clear headers and bullet lists, but lacks tabular data presentation or visual contrast.
rating_scale.5: Exceptional presentation using clean tables, bold highlights, and clear section hierarchy.
